text: The hand comes down on Borro's shield, and Jaeha, palms on Borro's back, pulls the whole blow through into himself.
He doesn't pass it on. He holds it, skin glowing white-gold, cracks of light up his arms, bones creaking.
Store: one strike at three hundred and forty percent. So heavy that his thirty seconds shrink to ten.
His bones have set the deadline, and the clock is already running.
To her, the blow has simply vanished. Her hand lifts away, confused, and Jaeha gives his team one destination: her head.
Every link he has lights up at once, and Moon Ahin's own cyan threads run out to her twelve husks.
Summons go first. Nib runs up her forearm, cutting a path through the barnacles.
Lyra shoots out the bars of her lantern, breaking the glare.
Moon Ahin conducts, and her twelve husks leap onto the leviathan's flank and lock together into a stair.
And Geum grabs Jaeha by the collar with her steel hand, grinning. She has a faster way up.
She throws him like a comet, straight at the white stair on the leviathan's flank.
Seven seconds left to hold.
From the light tower, Pim calls every step, like a navigator talking down a pilot.
He runs up the stair of husks, and they crack under his feet one by one.
Her other hand knocks the lower steps into the sea, Saebyeok among them, but he's already on her back.
Three seconds. He lands on top of her head, beside the long violet crack in her brow.
From up here he can see three fishing boats far out on the black sea, lost in a violet haze.
Pim's antennae turn toward her, and his eyes fill. There's still someone under the monster.
Deep in the crack, a warm light flickers like a candle, and a small voice asks him to bring them home.
Out there, an old fisherman peers into the haze. He can't see the lighthouse, or which way the harbour is.
Two seconds. His face softens. He isn't the one who stopped, he tells her, and her request is his now.
All the light in his body pours down his arm into his right fist, until it blazes like a small sun.
And for the first time in more than three hundred raids, Jaeha strikes with his own hand. Release.
The crack shatters, and the Hush pours out of her like smoke.
Her eye clears, from dull violet to a gentle sea-grey.
And her lantern burns white again. For one moment she is what she used to be: a lighthouse.
Her beam sweeps the sea, and the three lost boats turn toward it and come safely in.
On the pier, people who crept back watch them come home, hands over their mouths.
Pim is crying openly. She remembers her name, the one she had before the Hush: Oriel.
The trap rat with zero kills finally has one of his own, and it's S-grade.
The rewards roll in, Release among them, and the sea gate begins to close.
Oriel sinks slowly into the harbour and dissolves into light, and far out at sea, the gate closes.
And Jaeha falls thirty metres toward the black water, his right arm broken.
Lyra dives after him.
She catches him in the dark water and kicks for the light above.
Borro reaches down and hauls them both out, one in each hand.
Lyra wrings her braid out over him, smug. The merchant's tab with her keeps growing.
Out over the water, her core still glows. The window offers harvest, and nothing else.
Pim knows what she wants. Jaeha remembers the only time the window gave him a choice: he sent Nib's commander home.
And a Kanghan boat is racing toward the core.
Kanghan farms what it catches. That isn't happening to her.
So he presses harvest.
The core flies into his hand a second before their net reaches it. He cradles it and promises her he'll find that missing button.
The light inside the coral pulses once, slowly, like an answer.
On the barge, Han Sora laughs out loud. Kanghan just lost its prize, and she finds it hilarious.
By nine-thirty, the harbour is calm, and the breakwater is full of people.
Yerin's mint light can only start the healing. Jaeha thanks her like she has fixed everything.
And Seoa, crying and furious, holds out a bowl. Dinner was at seven. It's half past nine.
The aunties feed everyone on the breakwater: summons, husks, rescuers, fishermen and the whole neighbourhood.
Pim is buried in fish cakes by grateful aunties and fishermen. For once, his rank can wait.
Over six million people are watching.
And all along the harbour, the people of Busan raise their fists and chant for the Trap Rats.
Moon Ahin sits with all twenty-eight husks, cracked but home. She noticed what he gave back mid-fight.
Geum sits down beside him and nudges him with her steel elbow. The training offer still stands.
Geum laughs, and a window closes the quest: capacity a hundred and eighteen percent, body rating F-plus.
In Seoul, Director Baek watches the stream from his office.
The Association's deputy director stands in Kanghan's office like an employee, waiting for orders. Baek doesn't turn round.
Baek smiles at his reflection. He isn't worried about Jaeha getting stronger. He's counting on it.
His finger taps the violet core on his cane, once.
After midnight, everyone on the breakwater is asleep, except Pim.
Then his antennae snap upright, glowing.
Very far away, inside some gate, something small is tapping. Short, short, long.
He shakes the Operator awake. A frightened little signal, from somewhere behind a gate, in a scout's rhythm.
Nib's knives fall out of his hands and clatter on the stone.
Nib whispers a name from the Ninth Wall: Kett.
The young scout he sent running from the Ninth Wall with a sealed message, and a promise: go first, I'll be right behind you.
